propositions: A Jira issue's key changes when moved between projects, but its numeric id is immutable; rebar bindings keyed on the mutable key can silently detach when the old key stops resolving due to third-party movers failing to update the moved_issue_key table.

The fix persists the numeric id alongside the key in bindings (additive, not re-keying the store), and on a key lookup miss, retries by id and re-keys the binding to the issue's current key if found, updating the reverse index in the same operation.

Bindings written before this change continue to work unchanged with no migration: entries without a recorded id have no fallback and behave exactly as today, with id captured opportunistically on the next successful read.
The absence probe will not retire an issue reachable by its recorded numeric id, preventing silent detachment of moved issues.
The id fallback is only attempted after a key lookup fails; on a successful key resolve the fallback does not fire, preserving the happy path cost.
All existing jira_key-taking methods retain unchanged signature and semantics; the capture is a separate record_jira_id call to preserve Cloud bridge compatibility.
